content: Private consultants received £3.4bn from public organisations last year, a figure that remains significantly above levels seen before the pandemic, according to new data. This represents a 62% increase in spending by the government on consultants compared to 2019-20. Despite intentions from Keir Starmer’s government to reduce these costs, consultant spending has not decreased. Notably, KPMG recently secured a contract worth up to £223m to train civil servants, and since the Labour government took office, nearly £650m in new contracts have been awarded to consulting firms, many of which were agreed before the new administration. Critics, including Labour peer Prem Sikka, describe this reliance on consultants as excessive and question whether they provide genuine value to government work.
